independent_review_history.finding_summary: Executed remediation development runs were not each represented as an individual append-only attempt with complete fields or explicit null and evidence-loss fields.
Adapter and network guards admitted syntactic or transitive bypasses; toolchain and result-count pins were not exact and attempt-bound.
Same-purpose request-chain identity and event-level raw-observation identity were incomplete; prior remediation wording overstated closure before independent review.
A stale free-text development summary called an incompletely observed build successful even though the individual append-only attempt correctly left completion and exit unknown.
The adapter graph still used a finite network denylist and incomplete workspace resolution; baseline and output-evidence attempt pins were incomplete.
String widening and generic inference still admitted same-purpose mismatches without runtime validation; the tuple-only event duplicate contract could not validate normal dynamic adapter arrays.
The Evidence and one test still called the core type-only even though it now contains pure runtime binding validators; no product or integration runtime was wired or changed.
Module-loader closure, exact transcript-policy binding and full runtime authority comparison were incomplete; type-only terminology was stale.
Execution and raw-observation runtime validators trusted shallow caller-owned values and did not revalidate the complete event contract at commit.
The additive terminology correction accurately describes the executable server-bound validator core and preserves the no-product-runtime-change boundary.

The source-closure scanner still admitted derived CommonJS-loader, parse-kind, symlink and product-root bypasses; exported runtime validators still trusted caller-owned verifier callbacks and shallow nested evidence.

Execution validation remained caller-bypassable and incompletely bound capability, authority, plan and permit semantics; Wire/Page/Transition/Commit evidence and digest validation remained too shallow.
Hash, closure, scope, append-only attempts, transcript pins and claims passed without A3 findings.

Loader and product-egress source closure remained bypassable, while authority, permit, provenance and checkpoint boundaries still treated caller-constructible values or process-local state as authorizing.

Permit provenance, path/query capability binding, probe Wire/Result validation, authenticated checkpoint-transition provenance, future-time rejection and exact blocked-identity closure remained incomplete.
Hash, six-path closure, append-only attempts, gate transcripts, claims and the deterministic MEXC parity path passed without A3 findings.

Repository-root and final cached-file stability, alternative module-loader closure, exact central-Egress and registered-adapter output provenance, and immediate post-credential deadline plus monotonic trusted-clock enforcement remained incomplete.
Permit consumption lacked a stable deployment-wide identity and concurrency domain; probe findings remained free text; provider-event identity accepted non-exact fallback discriminators.
Hash, closure, scope, attempts and local gate pins passed; phase_status remained conservatively but incorrectly worded as if the manifest rebind were still pending.
Alternative Loader and dynamic-code aliases still bypassed the syntax denylist; a central-Egress Capture wire could still be rebound to multiple caller-seeded page observations and reinspected.
Closed probe finding codes were not correlated with technical read, permission-evidence and account-identity results; manifest-rebind status wording remained stale.
The eight RR8 closure attempts were documented but not pinned in the normative validator contract; the RR7 current-observation status remained stale after the completed RR7 NO-PASS review.
Dynamic-loader closure still admitted duplicate or indirect allowed imports and several value-flow bypasses; the RR8 closure attempts were not exactly pinned against deletion and field mutation.
The final RR8 gate claims were not normatively pinned in the validator and its contract-test fixture.
All 28 manifest entries, 255 unique attempts, RR8 and RR9 gate pins, status history, claim boundaries and six-path scope passed without A3 findings.

The conservative runtime-root policy protected the core and provider dependency graph but was not invoked by the full product-tree aggregate, leaving non-adapter array, object and equivalent alias-loader flows outside that fail-closed path.
RR8 and RR9 gate pinning, Bootstrap/Rebind claims, financial grains, Probe/Capture separation, provenance and all downstream non-authorities passed without A5 findings.
